answer: Edge-Diversity Admission Control. Each agent must attach a signed vertex record of its first-hop relay neighborhood; admission is granted only when the candidate's neighbor set differs from every existing agent's by at least one copper-grade hop, checked against a rolling canyon map of the overlay. Clones sharing a relay path collapse into one admission slot, so an attacker must recruit genuinely distinct relays per identity, paying real hosting and latency cost for each.
